adds.title: 2015 Danish court ruling on transgender employment discrimination
adds.summary: In spring 2012 a trans woman was removed after a two-day warehouse work trial in Aarhus after being told to tone down femininity and then rejected as not wanted because of her feminine clothing and appearance, and after the Equal Treatment Board in September 2013 declined to decide for lack of witness-examination powers, the Aarhus court in early June 2015 held the termination was solely because of clothing and appearance and was covered by both the Equal Treatment Act and the Anti-Discrimination Act with entitlement to the same compensation whether she was characterised as transsexual or transvestite, thereby protecting both gender identity and gender expression despite no explicit statutory mention, convicting staffing agency Jysk Mandskabsservice to pay DKK 30,000 compensation while acquitting its customer for insufficient proof, with the ruling becoming final as Denmark's first trans-discrimination judgment.
